reason: The measurements are right and the diagnosis and the fix are both wrong. Driven at 1440x960 (open owner-flight, click the first .b-grab): computed padding is 88px 16px 16px, panel top y=597, hidden .b-undo band 614-664, first ink 'WHAT IT IS' y=686, .b-editActs y=1034, .b-editDanger y=1085 - exactly as claimed. But the 88px is not what puts the foot below the fold. Moving the reserve does not change the panel's height (104px of padding either way) or its top (y=597, set by the rail stack under the 79-day horizon), so it cannot lift the panel's bottom edge at all; it only slides the content inside. I applied the proposed fix verbatim at runtime - padding 16/16/16/88, .b-undo reordered to last child, top:16px changed to bottom:16px - and measured: .b-editActs lands at y=962-1001, i.e. Done is still entirely below the 960px fold. The finding's headline benefit, 'Done and Delete rise 72px - back above the 960px fold at 1440', is false by 2px on the top edge and by the whole control in fact. The real cause of the off-fold foot is keepInBand (render-b.js:600), which returns early unless the panel is position:fixed, so at >=1280 the rail editor is never scrolled into view; padding is irrelevant to it. Worse, the fix regresses three things. (1) The reversibility bar goes off screen. Baseline: press +7 and the bar paints at y=614-708, fully visible. With the fix: y=1043-1137, entirely below the fold at both 1440x960 and 1280x900. The design explicitly pays for the opposite - 'the offer to take a change back is never off screen' (b.css, the max-width:1279 block) - and the fix breaks it at exactly the two widths where the panel already overruns the fold, which is the case the finding itself flags. (2) Tab order regresses from [Undo, title, date, -7, -1, +1, +7, Shown, Hidden, Done, Delete this moment] to [title, ..., Done, Delete this moment, Undo]: a keyboard owner reaching for undo must now tab past the one destructive control on the surface. (3) The silence is not removed, only relocated - at 390 and 768 the fix leaves an 89px void between 'Delete this moment' and the sheet's bottom edge, and at 1440 that void is off screen where it buys nothing. That leaves the aesthetic half: a documented, deliberate reserve (Round 1 paid for the stepper holding still under the pointer) whose placement has a functional reason, restated as a mistake. Taste, and the proposed trade is measurably worse.
sharpenedFix: Discard the move-to-the-foot fix. Two separable things are actually worth doing, neither of which is this finding. First, the reserve is undersized, not merely empty: at rail width (344px) the filled bar measures 94px tall against an 88px reserve, and because .b-undo carries an opaque background it paints straight over 'WHAT IT IS' - press +7 at 1440 and the first label of the panel disappears under the bar. Either raise the reserve to clear the wrapped bar at the narrowest column the panel is ever laid out in, or stop the bar wrapping by trimming its sentence. Second, if the resting band bothers a seat, occupy it rather than move it - the panel has provenance the owner never sees ('added 3 July', the moment's shown/hidden state) that could hold the band at rest and be replaced by the bar when a change is made, which keeps the reserve, keeps the bar on screen, keeps Undo first in tab order, and removes the silence. Separately and unrelated to padding: the off-fold foot at 1440/1280 is keepInBand's `if (getComputedStyle(panel).position !== "fixed") return;` - give the rail case its own branch so opening the editor brings its foot into view.
